1443.note: Winterthur ASC 876 (Buckingham's Watervliet Shaker hymnbook, dated 1830 not '18th-19th century'): scan images 35 and 44 show lines of an unknown glyph script set under music staves, matching the cataloguer's 'two hymns are written in code', with no decipherment found, though Shaker spirit-language script remains a possible alternative to a private cipher.

seen.where: Winterthur Library Digital Collections, https://digitalcollections.winterthur.org/documents/detail/2310 (viewer images 35 and 44 of 54 viewed in Chrome on 4 Nov 2026); finding aid http://winterthur.libraryhost.com/repositories/2/archival_objects/69 (ASC 876, 'Hymnbook, compiled by David Austin Buckingham, 1830').
seen.extent: One manuscript hymnbook, 54 images; glyph text seen on image 35 (seven short lines beside a staff) and image 44 (three glyph lines under music, the last line ending in a word in Latin letters); shorter coded marks end some hymns. The record dates the volume 1830 and places it at Watervliet, New York (the lead's '18th-19th century' is loose).
seen.cipher: Winterthur description: 'Few authors are given, although some of the poems end with something written in code. ... Two hymns are written in code, and something (a name?) is written in code at the end of some hymns.' On the leaves the code is a cursive, shorthand-like symbol script in word-like groups where lyrics would stand; no plaintext is written on or beside it. Whether it is a private substitution or a Shaker 'spirit language' script was not settled.
